title.value: Bridging the Gap Between Offline and Online Reinforcement Learning Evaluation Methodologies
title.justification: The title clearly indicates that the paper focuses on the methodologies to evaluate offline and online reinforcement learning.
title.quote: Bridging the Gap Between Offline and Online Reinforcement Learning Evaluation Methodologies

extractions.description: This paper proposes a sequential approach to evaluate offline reinforcement learning algorithms by using data efficiency as a metric, termed Sequential Evaluation (SeqEval). The authors detail how this evaluation provides insights into the algorithms' data efficiency and robustness to dataset distribution changes. The paper further demonstrates this approach through experiments comparing different offline RL algorithms.

primary_category.justification: The paper primarily focuses on evaluation methodologies in reinforcement learning, which does not directly relate to eco-responsible categories like climate change or pollution.
primary_category.quote: This paper, we propose a sequential approach to evaluate offline RL algorithms as a function of the training set size and thus by their data efficiency.

secondary_categories.justification: The scope of the paper is technical and related to reinforcement learning algorithms, without direct connections to eco-responsible themes.
secondary_categories.quote: While online RL algorithms are typically evaluated as a function of the number of environment interactions, there isn’t a single established protocol for evaluating offline RL methods.

primary_sub_category.justification: There are no direct references to sub-categories under eco-responsible themes, as the content is more focused on reinforcement learning methodologies.
primary_sub_category.quote: The existence of logged data from industrial applications provides ample data to train agents in simulation till they achieve good performance and then can be trained on real hardware.

secondary_sub_categories.justification: The sub-categories of eco-responsibility do not apply to this paper which focuses on technical evaluation strategies for RL.
secondary_sub_categories.quote: Offline RL methods tackle this problem by leveraging previously collected data to bootstrap the learning process towards a good policy.

new_primary_category.justification: This paper introduces a new evaluation methodology for offline RL, which is a significant step in understanding and improving the data efficiency of RL algorithms, a topic distinct from existing eco-responsible categories.
new_primary_category.quote: We propose to evaluate algorithms as a function of available data instead of just reporting final performance or plotting learning curves over a number of gradient steps.

new_primary_sub_category.justification: The contribution of the paper lies in the introduction of Sequential Evaluation (SeqEval) as a method for assessing offline RL algorithms, which does not fit into existing eco-responsible sub-categories.
new_primary_sub_category.quote: This approach allows us to study the sample efficiency and robustness of offline RL algorithms to distribution shifts.
